title: dev.qory.run.refused
description: The run did not start. Emitted in place of dev.qory.run.started, the run's first event after the ping where there is one, heartbeats aside, and its last, by the session. A gateway refuses the session's run request, with a code in its answer on the link, unsigned and authenticated by the transport: the refusal opens no run at the gateway, the session records the run.refused it received, its code and names, in its own record alone, and nothing reaches the server for it. A session that fails after the gateway's run answer and before its process starts posts its run.refused on the link: the gateway holds that run, and delivers it. Events carry names and ids alone, and no value but the run credential's own in a gateway's refusal that names one.

code.description: Why the run did not start: a refusal code of Forager, of qory, of the server, or of a gateway that verifies a run credential, the one the refusal's body contained: the server's in its signed answer, a gateway's in its answer on the link, unsigned. The codes Forager, qory, the server and a gateway share are the list the schema holds the code to when there is no status; the session writes the code of a gateway's 410 that closed the run before it started, run_closed, session_lost, batch_refused, credential_expired, stopped, credential_check_unreachable or credential_check_invalid, with status 410, and the code of a gateway's refusal it received: credential_check_unreachable for a gateway's 503 and credential_check_invalid for a gateway's 502 among them. A code that came from the server comes with its status, and is kept as the server's body contained it, one the list does not hold yet included: a receiver shows a code it does not know as it is.

names.description: The names the refusal concerns: variables, tools, images, paths, an earlier or another run's id, or the names a server's or a gateway's coded refusal lists. A name never carries a value, except the run credential's own value in target_differs_from_credential and differs_from_credential: there each name is <member>=<value>, the member the session sent, labels.<key> or about.details.<key>, then = and the value the run credential holds, such as labels.forge=example-forge.

status.description: The HTTP status of the answer, when the code came from the server, or from a gateway's 410 that ended the run before it started.
